- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 1–1.5% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price > 75% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model typically peaks 2–3 days after true price peak; adjust by adding 1–2 days of lagged sentiment momentum to forecast tail.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model fails to capture volatility; apply smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted average before forecasting.
